policies.summary: Local governments may not adopt zoning that prohibits solar generating stations (over 1 MW, wholesale or community solar) or deny site plans that meet the state siting standards, must expedite review, and must treat projects of 5 MW or less as a permitted use, subject to the growth-area and priority preservation exceptions in MD-other-1.

Local governments may not adopt zoning that prohibits front-of-the-meter energy storage or deny site plans that meet the state requirements, and must expedite review and adopt standard review processes.

Ground-mounted solar over 5 MW may not be sited on land that on 2025-01-01 was in a Tier 1 or Tier 2 growth area, a medium or high density residential area, or a mixed-use area with homes, and solar in a priority preservation area established before 2025 is capped at 5 percent of that area's acreage.

Grid-connected generating stations need a certificate of public convenience and necessity (or an exemption or distributed generation certificate) from the Public Service Commission, and front-of-meter storage needs Commission approval; for wholesale or community solar of 1 to 2 MW the local jurisdiction checks the state siting standards instead. Counties still issue local permits but may not require conditional use or special exception approval.

Solar generating stations over 1 MW (other than agrivoltaics) must keep 150 feet from homes and 100 feet from property lines, keep fencing at most 20 feet tall and 50 feet from roads, provide a vegetative buffer up to 35 feet wide, emit no visible light at night, and average no more than 15 feet in height; a county siting agreement may set looser terms.
